## Teaching points

1. Fever or sore throat in a patient taking a thionamide is agranulocytosis until proven otherwise: stop the drug and check a CBC with differential (2016 ATA hyperthyroidism guideline).
2. Thyroid storm is a clinical diagnosis; a Burch–Wartofsky score of 45 or more is highly suggestive, and hormone levels do not separate storm from uncomplicated thyrotoxicosis.
3. Standard therapy is a beta-blocker, a thionamide, iodine given at least an hour after the thionamide, a glucocorticoid, cooling and treatment of the precipitant.
4. After thionamide-induced agranulocytosis the other thionamide is contraindicated (cross-reactivity), and iodine without thionamide cover can worsen thyrotoxicosis; bridge with beta-blockade, glucocorticoid and cholestyramine to early thyroidectomy.
5. Neutropenic fever needs immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics; avoid aspirin for fever in thyroid storm because it displaces hormone from binding proteins.
